uncited: *   **3D Gaussian:** Stores $p_i$ (3 floats), $\Sigma_i$ (6 floats, symmetric positive definite), $\rho_i$ (1 float).
Apply a local affine transformation to each Gaussian to map it to ray space.
Integrate the 3D Gaussian along the ray path (z-axis in ray space).
Calculate the central density $\hat{\rho}_i$ of the resulting 2D Gaussian.
Render the projection by summing the contributions of all 2D Gaussians.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(M \cdot N)$ where $M$ is the number of Gaussians and $N$ is the number of pixels covered by the Gaussians.
The transformation and projection steps are $O(M)$.
*   **When to use:** When simulating X-ray CT projections from 3D Gaussian fields.
*   **When not to use:** For standard visible-light rendering where alpha-compositing is appropriate.
The transformation module is based on the Ewa Splatting approach [69] for local affine approximation.
